object_description: three separate buildings linked along a path, with a low pavilion-like wing
design_condition: the three buildings are strung along the path so that they form a common entrance square at the junction and then a recreation area, with the gymnasium sunk and its roof used as a playground

positive: The buildings are linked so that they form a common entrance square at the junction and a recreation area beyond
The more public uses are concentrated in the first building at the square
The pavilion-like wing along the tree-lined avenue has an optimal connection between its outdoor area and the park
The common centre with hall, kitchen, library and day school is functionally well designed
The entrance square is easily accessible from both sides
The special rooms have a direct exit to the playground on the gymnasium roof
The pavilion-like basic level responds well to the required use and allows permeability from the housing to the park
The simple concept is convincing pedagogically and functionally thanks to its structure
Public uses sit in the most public part, the classroom wing where building depth is available, the basic level where contact with ground and park is closest
The division into three separate structures creates controlled in-between spaces without the complex falling apart
The separate buildings have a clean structural solution
The gymnasium ceiling is designed with an interesting truss construction
The sports room programme is complete and well organised
negative: Housing both elementary school stages along the square is not entirely unproblematic in urban planning terms
The roof gardens as break areas would hardly work, as the available space is very limited
The allocation of the group rooms is rather unfavourable
One break area would have to be used by four classrooms
The escape route situation was not considered feasible as proposed and would have to be revised
The escape route concept of the gymnasium also still needs revision
The transgression of the federal building line would have to be corrected
The proposed facades are far too vaguely formulated and leave too much room for interpretation
The details cannot demonstrate the same quality as the urban and operational concept
The completely buried gymnasium provides little stimulation and social control in the evenings and at weekends
The special rooms in front of the break halls are clear but not exactly inspiring for school use
The allocation of classrooms to three roof gardens proves relatively rigid, and the access knot can hardly be solved
The project is rated as costly in terms of maintenance and building cleaning
Some necessary lift connections in the basic level wing are missing
